answer: Ferrous Trace Locking. Each agent identity must submit a hardware-attested timestamped trace of a physical process (e.g., a ferrous part's corrosion curve) that decays uniquely; the ocean of submissions is checked against a crystal lattice index of prior traces, and any near-duplicate is rejected. An attacker cloning one capture pays full sensor and notary cost per identity, plus the cost of generating genuinely distinct physical histories, which scales linearly with sock-puppet count.
